title: Download and preparation time

response: Budget one download session, then a few minutes to extract and copy to the drive. After that it is ready forever: plug in, tick boxes, run. The prep is a one-time cost, unlike the hour you lose on every manual setup.

title: Does it include Windows ISOs
patterns: does it come with an iso
can i install windows with it
response: No. This is a post-install toolkit, not an operating system image. You install Windows yourself from your own media or licence, then use the toolkit to set the machine up. It does not include Windows ISOs, keys or activators.
followup: Want to know what it does right after the install?

title: Cracks and activators
response: No. The toolkit ships legitimate installers for freely distributed, trial or vendor-supplied software — and our own automation tools. It contains no cracks, activators or keygens, and licensing each program for your client is handled normally.
followup: Do you want to know which Office versions are included?

title: Keeping the package current
patterns: how do i keep it updated
how do i refresh the installers
do i have to rebuild the usb
response: You drive it from the updater panel inside the toolkit: it lists each program with its last update date and drops the newest installer into the right folder on the drive. No rebuilding from scratch and no extra charge.
followup: Anything else technical you want to check?

title: MInstAll launcher
patterns: how does the batch installer work
response: MInstAll is the launcher at the centre of the toolkit. It opens with every category and program listed, lets you tick what you need — including a select-all option — and then runs the whole queue in sequence with no per-program intervention.
followup: Would you like to see the interface screenshots?

title: Installation speed on the bench
patterns: how long does the queue take
can i install while doing something else
response: The queue runs unattended, start to finish, so your hands are free for the next machine. That is the real gain: instead of supervising setups, you prep the next job and come back to a finished machine.
followup: Would you like the purchase link?

title: Space needed on the client machine

does it install onto the pc
do i install the toolkit on the pc
response: The toolkit itself runs from the USB drive and takes no meaningful space on the client machine. Only the programs you choose to install end up on the hard drive, exactly as if you had installed them manually.
followup: Anything else about how it runs?

title: Utilities included
response: Dozens: 7-Zip, WinRAR, FileZilla, PDF readers, download managers, media players, codec packs, benchmarking and diagnostic helpers, remote access tools and system cleanup utilities — the everyday kit of a repair bench.

title: Who it is for
response: It is made for PC repair shops, IT support techs, freelancers and anyone who reinstalls Windows regularly — including people who do it as a side job or for their own machines. If you touch more than a couple of PCs a month, it pays for itself.

title: How it is tested
response: Every installer is checked and organised by category, and the package is maintained continuously — new versions, new titles and fixes come through our own updater rather than being left as-is after release.

title: Windows 11
patterns: does it support the latest windows
response: Yes. Windows 11 is fully supported — the launcher, the driver panel and the updater all work there, and the tweaks list includes Windows 11 specific items like the classic context menu.
followup: Anything else about your machines?

title: Windows 10
patterns: will it work on an older windows 10 pc
response: Yes — Windows 10 is one of the main targets. Program installation and offline drivers behave the same way as on Windows 11, including on machines that have been running for years.
followup: Do you also service older Windows versions?

title: Windows 7
response: Many tools in the package still run on Windows 7, which helps with older machines that come in for repair, but the full flow is designed and tested for Windows 10 and 11. Treat Windows 7 support as best-effort rather than guaranteed.
followup: Anything else about the machines you service?

title: Laptops
patterns: will it work on my laptop
response: Yes — laptops are the most common case for this toolkit. The driver panel handles the usual problem areas: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, touchpad, audio and power management that Windows does not cover on its own.
followup: Do you want to check the driver details?

title: Desktops and custom builds
response: Desktops and custom builds are well covered, mainboards included. The driver panel reads the chipset and controller IDs, so it does not rely on the brand name of the machine.
followup: Anything else you want to confirm?

title: Which Windows versions overall
response: Primary support is **Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit**. Most 32-bit installers are also present, and a number of tools still work on Windows 7. When in doubt about a specific machine, ask us before buying — {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.
followup: Would you like the purchase link?

title: Antivirus warnings
response: Bulk installers and driver packs are a classic false-positive trigger, because they run many setup files in sequence. If Windows Defender or your antivirus quarantines something during a run, restore it from the quarantine list and add an exception for the toolkit folder. The files come from the vendors' own installers.
followup: Do you want the exact steps to add an exception?
